title: The Teenagers Who Stole the Next Xbox

lines.text: In twenty-thirteen, two young men walked into a secure building at Microsoft's headquarters, and walked out carrying the next Xbox. Nobody stopped them. And that wasn't even the worst part.
Rewind. A few years earlier, a handful of teenagers met online. They lived in Canada, America and Australia, and they shared one obsession. Xbox.
They started by cracking open their own consoles, to run games and code Microsoft never allowed. They called themselves the Xbox Underground.
Then they went further. From their bedrooms, they slipped into the networks of the companies making the games. Epic. Valve. Activision. And Microsoft itself.
They grabbed Call of Duty and Gears of War before release. And a break-in at a small studio handed them something stranger: Apache helicopter training software, built for the United States Army.
Inside Microsoft, they found the biggest prize of all. Secret plans for the next Xbox, codenamed Durango. Enough to build their own copy, months before anyone could buy one.

But plans weren't enough. They wanted the real thing. So in September twenty-thirteen, two accomplices used a copied badge to walk into a secure building in Redmond, and left with three unreleased Xbox development kits.
They wandered the halls, and no one noticed. Prosecutors later valued everything the group took at between one hundred and two hundred million dollars.
But the FBI was already on their trail. In March twenty-fourteen, the group's leader, David Pokora, a twenty-two year old from near Toronto, tried to cross the border into New York.
At the crossing in Lewiston, he was arrested. Pokora pleaded guilty, in what the Justice Department believed was the first conviction of a foreign hacker for stealing American trade secrets.
He got eighteen months in prison. Two other members got eighteen months and two years. The youngest, who helped plan the badge job, got probation.
And one Australian member fled to the Czech Republic, where he's a citizen. America can't extradite him.

It took a network break-in to find the next Xbox, but just one copied badge to carry it out the door. Badges get cloned, just like passwords get stolen. If someone follows you through a secure door at work, ask who they are. Follow for more true stories of internet crime.

facts.claim: Group breached Microsoft, Epic Games, Valve, Activision and Zombie Studios 2011-2013; took pre-release Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3 and Gears of War 3, Xbox One technical data, and Apache helicopter training software made for the US Army; enough to build a counterfeit Xbox One
Loss valued between $100 million and $200 million

September 2013: physical theft of three non-public Xbox One development kits from a secure building on Microsoft's Redmond campus, brokered by Alcala and Pokora, using a copied badge; they walked around undetected

Pokora, 22, of Mississauga, Ontario, viewed as the leader, arrested 28 March 2014 at the Lewiston, New York port of entry; DOJ: believed to be the first conviction of a foreign-based hacker for stealing US trade secrets
Sentences: Pokora 18 months; Nesheiwat 18 months; Leroux 24 months; Alcala (youngest, 18 when charged) three years supervised release
Australian member (Dylan Wheeler) fled to the Czech Republic, holds Czech citizenship, cannot be extradited
